critical_code_review_comments: server.py now at 1231 lines (grew ~116 for /kits + /auth/session). Monolithic but still readable. Splitting into routers (auth, kits, receipts, products) remains a non-blocking tech-debt item.

GET /kits/{id} is unauthenticated against warehouse scope — any logged-in user can read any kit by id. list_kits scopes via scope_wh(user, warehouse_id) but get_kit does not call ensure_wh_access. Not a security issue in practice (kit payload exposes bin counts which are already read-only via /bins), but inconsistent with the write-side policy. Noted only.
enrich_kit does N product-lookups via db.stock.find + db.bins.find_one per item. For small kits (<=10 items) this is fine; batch via $in would be nicer at scale.

AuthProvider.extractSessionId uses a regex on window.location.href that strips &-adjacency badly in replace (/[?#&]session_id=[^&#]+&?/ then '$1'). If session_id is the last param after other params (e.g. '?foo=bar&session_id=xyz'), the leading '&' is captured but '$1' is the first char ('?'), yielding '?foo=bar?' briefly — minor; the subsequent trailing '[?#&]$' trim handles the final char only. Not observed in prod flow since the Google redirect uses only session_id.
login.tsx: Google button sits beside Sign-in with no 'during login' disabled state coupling — ok but if user double-clicks Google while sign-in is in-flight, two network ops race. Not blocking.

kit/[id].tsx: delete uses a window.confirm/Alert pattern; after DELETE the console shows a 404 Failed-to-load — this is a react-query refetch of /kits/{id} after invalidation, which is expected since the resource no longer exists. No user-visible error.
